title: [Chapitre] VII. Analysis situs (troisième mouture) : notes manuscrites (23-26/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: in this third version of 'Analysis situs' (June 1986), Grothendieck is building an order-theoretic, point-free axiomatics for 'tame' spaces. The basic structure is an 'atelier' (F, ≤, ≪). F is a set of 'figures'. ≤ means 'is a subfigure of'. ≪ means 'lies in the shadow (omb) of'. L is the set of minimal elements ('lieux', loci). On the previous page he wrote axioms Prat dis 1'–6' for the 'polyhedral/spacious' case, using a symmetric, irreflexive disjunction relation ∥ on L. Here X̃ = {Y ≤ X}, omb(X) = {x ∈ L : x ≪ X}, and x ≪° X means x lies in the interior of omb(X).

Page 53, part 1 (axiom Prat pol). The polyhedral case needs one more axiom. For every X in M, the down-set X̃ must be 'polyhedral': if Y, Z ≤ X have a common lower bound, then Inf^≤(Y,Z) exists, i.e. Ỹ ∩ Z̃ has a greatest element. This is the combinatorial shadow of 'the intersection of two faces of a polytope is a face (or empty)'.

NB: then Sup^≤(Y,Z) exists inside X̃ (as the inf of the common upper bounds), but not necessarily in M. So each X̃, with a bottom adjoined, is a lattice, like the face lattice of a polytope.

Part 2 (Remark: the 'trivial' presentation). Take any poset (M, ≤), put ≪ := ≤ and x ∥ y :⇔ x ≠ y. Then X ≪° Y ⇔ X = Y. All the axioms Prat 1–6 hold except divisibility (Prat dis 2': every X has some locus x with x ≪° X). That axiom fails as soon as X is not minimal.

Motivating example: M = the simplices of an abstract simplicial complex (S, M ⊂ P_f(S)), ordered by inclusion. The figures are the subcomplexes, i.e. the closed (downward-closed) subsets: the Alexandrov topology on the face poset.

At the level of figures:
- F = Pf(M, ≤), the down-sets.
- F ≪ G ⇔ F ⊆ G, and the condition written 'F ⋡ G' always holds.
- F ∥ G ⇔ F ∩ G = ∅.
- At D, At C (spéc), At Fil and At sépar hold.
- At L2 amounts to 'every X is above a minimal element' — 'not worrying'.
- At L3 holds, since distinct loci are disjoint.
- So the only failing axiom is At L1, divisibility.

Role: divisibility is exactly what separates 'continuum-like' geometric realizations, where loci are dense in every figure, from purely combinatorial cell posets. A margin note calls the simplicial example 'préoccupant' for the notion of locus.
errors: The image appears to say 'si {X,Y} est majoré et minoré' and 'X̃ ∩ Ỹ'. Mathematically it must be {Y,Z} (both ≤ X) and Ỹ ∩ Z̃. This is a slip, in the manuscript or in the transcription.

At L2 ('every element is above a minimal element') can fail for a non-well-founded infinite poset. Grothendieck dismisses this as unproblematic, which is fine for finite or simplicial M but not for an 'arbitrary' poset, as the remark literally says.

ideas.what: Polyhedrality axiom: in each down-set X̃, bounded-below pairs have an infimum, so X̃ (with bottom) is a lattice — the face-lattice property 'intersection of faces is a face'.
ideas.modern_name: Lattice condition on intervals of a cell/face poset (polyhedral complexes, CW posets, face lattices of polytopes)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical polytope theory; CW posets Björner (1984)
ideas.where_published: Tame topology programme only sketched in Esquisse d'un programme §5–6; this axiomatics unpublished

ideas.what: Trivial presentation of any poset (≪=≤, ∥ = ≠) gives a structure satisfying all atelier axioms except divisibility. Example: face poset of a simplicial complex with subcomplexes = Alexandrov-closed sets.
ideas.modern_name: Face poset / Alexandrov (finite T0) space of a simplicial complex
ideas.usually_credited_to: Alexandrov (1937); McCord (1966) for finite spaces and simplicial complexes

ideas.what: Divisibility axiom (every figure has a locus in its interior) singled out as the precise axiom separating geometric (continuum) realizations from combinatorial ones.
ideas.modern_name: Density of points / no isolated cells; cf. 'atomless' vs 'atomic' in point-free topology
ideas.usually_credited_to: No specific attribution in this form

missed.claim: Grothendieck observes that the order-theoretic atelier axiomatics, applied to a face poset with its Alexandrov topology (finite T0 spaces), satisfies everything except divisibility. This implicitly links his tame-topology axioms to the finite-space/McCord picture, where the face poset models the homotopy type of the realization. He does not draw this link, and the literature on finite spaces does not connect to his ateliers.
missed.quote: Alors tous les axiomes sont satisfaits, sauf le seul axiome de divisibilité
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It suggests a formal 'realization' functor from posets (failing divisibility) to divisible ateliers, e.g. by barycentric subdivision iterated to a dense limit. This would be a point-free analogue of geometric realization within o-minimal/tame topology.

missed.claim: The margin flags the simplicial example as 'préoccupant' for the notion of 'lieux', but the issue is not resolved on the page. How combinatorial complexes should be accommodated (or excluded) in the theory of loci remains open here.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This bears on any attempt to reconstruct the unpublished 1986 tame-topology axiomatics as a working theory.

deep.surprise_reason: Routine example-checking within an unpublished axiomatic project. The polyhedral lattice axiom and the face-poset example are standard. The mild interest is that divisibility is isolated as the sole axiom distinguishing combinatorial from geometric models.
transcription_corrections: 'si {X, Y} est majoré et minoré' should mathematically read {Y, Z}, and 'X̃ ∩ Ỹ' should read Ỹ ∩ Z̃.
'(x ∥_c y)' — the subscript is more likely L (∥_L, as on p. 52) than c.
'Pr. LL2'' probably refers to the divisibility axiom Prat dis 2' (equivalently At L1 at the end of the page).
'Ay [?] relations "trivial" une préstation [?] ≪ ? [?] que' probably reads 'Appelons "triviale" une prestation (présentation) ≪ telle que'.
'ensemble de toutes les parties fermées dans F' — the 'dans F' begins the next clause ('dans F, F ≪ G ⇔ F ≤ G ...').
'Prenant F' is probably 'Pour ce F' / 'Prenant pour F'.
